overview: Tuberculosis is an infectious disease caused by bacteria that most often affects the lungs, spreading through the air when people with TB cough, sneeze or spit. It is preventable and curable, but can be fatal without treatment. About a quarter of the global population is estimated to have been infected with TB bacteria.
transmission: airborne transmission through coughing, sneezing or spitting
prevention: get screened for TB if at increased risk
complete full course of TB preventive treatment
use respirators and well-ventilated spaces in healthcare facilities
key_facts: 1.23 million people died from tuberculosis in 2024
10.7 million people fell ill with TB worldwide in 2024
83 million lives saved since 2000 through global efforts to combat TB
only about 2 in 5 people with drug-resistant TB accessed treatment in 2024
TB is the world’s leading cause of death from a single infectious agent
